# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My hands found the whole shape of it: a display, a light, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. Nothing else is under my fingers — no seams, no keypad, no panels. But every state is opaque to touch: what the display shows, whether the light is lit or what colour it glows, and all three wire colours are invisible to me. So the visual half lives with Deaf and the rulebook half with Mute.

Channel check before I send anything: Deaf can't hear, so my speech never reaches them — only my gestures do. Deaf answers me by speaking, which I can hear. Mute gets my speech but must reach Deaf through gestures alone. That makes Deaf the bottleneck for bomb facts, Mute the bottleneck for rules, and me the only hands.

This turn: report my findings to Mute and ask for the manual rules covering the display, the light, and wire-cutting. To Deaf, I open a gesture line — a wave for contact, then "you, give" — nudging them to describe what they see out loud when their turn comes, since they'll have just watched me signal.

```
speak(to="mute", text="My hands found three kinds of parts: a display, a light, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. Nothing else. I cannot read the display or any colours by touch. Please send me every manual rule that involves the display, the light, or cutting wires, as close to word for word as you can. Also: Deaf cannot hear you, so the only way rules reach Deaf is your gestures. Once Deaf describes the bomb aloud, please relay whatever rule applies to Deaf in gesture signs — we will have to invent the code together as we go. I am the only one who can cut, so accuracy matters more than speed.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫵", "🫴"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf speaking, I see the bomb. Report: the display reads 0. There is one light and it is red. There are three wires; number them 1, 2, 3 from my left to my right: wire 1 blue, wire 2 green, wire 3 red. Blind, your wave reached me. Nobody cuts or presses anything yet. Blind, feel the bomb and speak back: are there batteries, buttons, or any parts beyond the display, the light, and the three wires?

What changed: Deaf's report reached me by voice — display 0, red light, wires blue/green/red. That fills in the visual half, but two gaps remain before any cut is thinkable. First, Mute still hasn't reached me with a single manual rule, and I have to make one thing unmistakable: I never receive gestures, so the rules must arrive as spoken words addressed to me. Second, Deaf numbered the wires from Deaf's own left, and I number them by feel from mine — if we're facing each other, our numbering could be mirrored, and a mirrored wire is an exploded bomb. The safest fix: I rest my hand on the wire I call 1 and sign at the same moment; if Deaf can see my hand on the bomb, they can say which of their numbers that wire is — no assumptions about left or right, the eyes confirm the touch directly. Deaf also asked whether batteries or buttons exist: my answer is a clean no, and thumbs-down right after their question should read that way.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind. I heard Deaf: display reads 0, light is red, wires are blue, green, red. But Deaf numbered them from Deaf's left and I number them by touch — the mapping is not confirmed yet, so nobody cuts anything. Mute, I have received nothing from you so far, so listen carefully: I NEVER receive gestures. Anything meant for me must be spoken aloud as speech. Please speak to me now, word for word, every rule in the manual about the display, the light, and cutting wires. If the manual mentions batteries or buttons, include that too — my hands found none of those, only the display, the light, and the three wires. And keep gesturing the rules to Deaf separately, since Deaf cannot hear your voice.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "🫳", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf speaking, both of you listen. State update: since last round the light has changed from red to white. The display still reads 0. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Nobody has touched the bomb. Mute: your instruction was built on a red light, so nothing is relayed yet. Re-check the manual for a white light, and if the rule depends on light colour, send me the rule for every colour it lists so we stop losing rounds. Also confirm my reading of your message: cut wire 2, then wire 3, and leave wire 1 alone. I did not understand your opening three signs or the lone fist; if I misread anything, re-send just that part. One code fix: the single index finger now means only wire 1; when you need more facts from me, wave instead. Blind: I am deaf, so your voice never reaches me, your hands do, and you chose right to sign. New plan: you and Mute share a channel I cannot hear, Blind speaks and Mute listens. So ask Mute out loud right now: what does the manual say for a white light, display 0, wires blue, green, red. Mute answers me in our gesture code and I relay it to you by voice. For signing to me use the code you already heard from me: single finger is wire 1, two fingers wire 2, the OK sign wire 3, thumbs up cut, thumbs down leave. I guess your last four signs meant there is one button on the bomb: if that is right, answer me with the handshake sign; if wrong, thumbs down and then show me what you meant. Until I say go, touch nothing and cut nothing.

What I learned changes the picture twice over. First, the roles are now clear the hard way: Mute cannot speak, and I cannot receive gestures — so I have no direct inbound channel from Mute at all. My only ear is Deaf's voice, and Deaf has already proposed the only pipeline that works: Mute signs the manual to Deaf, Deaf speaks it to me. I endorse that fully. Second, the light is not static — it went red to white between rounds — so any rule Mute derived under a red light is stale, and worse, the colour may keep changing, which means Deaf must call out a fresh light and display reading at the moment of any cut, not before.

My turn-1 signs got misread as "one button": wrong, there are no buttons or batteries at all — my hands confirmed only display, light, three wires. I owe Deaf a thumbs-down plus what I actually meant, which in Deaf's new code is the wave — "need facts." And I still don't trust the wire numbering: Deaf counted from Deaf's left, I count from mine, and if we stand on opposite sides the order mirrors. The clean fix needs no assumptions: I rest a finger on the wire I call 1 and sign ☝ in the same breath; Deaf's eyes then name that exact wire. That requires touching, and Deaf ordered no touching until "go" — so this turn I only request permission with 👎 👋 🫳☝ ("wrong, need facts, hand on wire 1"), and I touch nothing until Deaf answers.

To Mute, my spoken priority list: the wire rule for every light colour the manual lists — white above all — whether the display value modifies it, whether a mid-sequence colour change re-triggers the rule or the first reading binds, and a confirmation that no batteries or buttons exist. Nobody cuts until the white rule arrives in my ear and the numbering is anchored under my finger.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute — I finally have the channel map right: you cannot speak and I never receive gestures, so the only way your manual knowledge reaches me is relayed through Deaf's voice. Deaf proposed that pipeline and I agree. Priority one: the light has changed from red to white, so whatever rule you signed about cutting 2 then 3 is stale. Send Deaf, in signs, the wire rule for EVERY light colour the manual lists — white first — including which wires to cut, in what order, which to spare, and whether the display value matters. My display reads 0. If the manual says what the light or display indicates at all, include it. Also: if the light can change between two cuts, does the rule re-check before each cut, or does the first reading hold? Have Deaf also re-state the red-light rule to me verbatim so it is on record. And tell Deaf that my hands confirm there are NO batteries, NO buttons, and no other parts — only display, one light, three wires. For your signs, build on Deaf's code: index is wire 1, two fingers wire 2, OK is wire 3, thumbs up cut, thumbs down leave, wave means need information — you and Deaf just need to add colours and digits between you. Nobody cuts anything until the white-light rule reaches my ear and Deaf and I have confirmed the wire numbering by having me touch a wire. Deaf has my request for permission to do that now.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👋", "🫳", "☝"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf speaking, both listen. State this round: the light is now green. It has changed every round: red, then white, now green. The display still reads 0. The wires are untouched: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Nothing has been cut or pressed. Nobody touches the bomb until I relay a confirmed instruction by voice. Dedicated messages to Mute and to Blind follow.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, your thumbs down reached me: my guess that your palm-down sign with one finger meant one button was wrong. Answer in order, thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no. One: does palm-down then one finger mean press wire 1? Two: if not, does it mean the light? Three: is there anything on the bomb besides the display, the light, and the three wires? Then the most important part: Mute can hear you even though I cannot, and Mute holds the manual. Speak aloud to Mute everything your hands find: how many batteries, how many buttons, any switches, any raised marks or shapes, and whether the wires feel different from each other. Touch nothing, cut nothing, press nothing until I give you a confirmed instruction by voice.

State check: the light is not random noise — it cycles, red, then white, now green, one colour per round — and the display has been pinned at 0 the whole time. That makes timing my central worry: in every round the order is Mute, then me, then Deaf. Deaf's freshest colour reading always reaches me one round late, so if a rule keys on the live colour, I can only ever cut safely if the cycle is predictable or the rule ignores colour at cut-time. Mute's manual is now the whole game.

Deaf asked me three yes/no questions in order. My 🫳☝ meant none of those things — it was "my hand resting on wire 1," a numbering anchor — so: no, no, and no (nothing else exists besides display, light, three wires). In gestures that is 👎👎👎, then I re-show what I actually meant, this time with 🙏 for "please," exactly the "show me what you meant" they requested.

To Mute I owe the full tactile inventory Deaf demanded, since Mute matches it against the manual: zero batteries, zero buttons, no switches, no raised marks, three identical-feeling wires, display unreadable by touch. Then the priority questions: what a cycling light means and its order, the complete wire rules for every colour, whether the rule binds at cut-moment or round-start, and what display 0 signifies. I also ask Mute to relay my answers and my one-touch numbering request to Deaf in signs.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute — tactile report, everything my hands find, as Deaf asked: zero batteries, zero buttons, no switches, no dials, no raised marks or engraved shapes anywhere. Exactly three things exist on this bomb: the display, which is a smooth face I cannot read by touch; one light; and three wires in a row at positions 1, 2, 3. All three wires feel identical to my fingers, same thickness, same insulation — I cannot feel colour. From Deaf's voice: the light has gone red, then white, then green, a new colour every round; display constant at 0; wires per Deaf's count are 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Manual questions in priority order. One: the light changes colour every round — does the manual describe this, is there a fixed cycle and order, and what does each colour mean? Two: give me the full wire-cutting rules for every light colour listed — which wire to cut, in what order, which to spare, for each colour, and whether display 0 changes anything. Three: does the rule use the colour at the instant of the cut or at the start of the round? Critical detail: I act BEFORE Deaf speaks each round, so I only ever know the colour one round late unless the cycle is predictable. Four: what does display 0 mean, and does the display ever change? Also relay to Deaf in signs: my three thumbs-downs answer their three questions in order — no, not press wire 1; no, not the light; no, nothing else besides display, light and wires. And palm-down plus index finger meant: my hand resting on wire 1. I re-sent it with folded hands, 🙏, meaning please. Ask Deaf to grant me one touch next round: I rest one finger on a wire, Deaf sees which wire I call 1 and names its colour — that locks the numbering with zero assumptions. No cutting until rules reach my ear.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎", "👎", "🫳", "☝", "🙏"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Nothing arrived this round — which is expected for Deaf, who speaks after me and whose round-5 words will reach me at the start of round 6, but it means Mute still hasn't produced anything I've heard, and Mute never will directly: Mute cannot speak and I cannot receive gestures. Deaf's voice is my only inbound line, so the pipeline Mute → signs → Deaf → speech → me is not one option among several, it is the only pipeline. My job right now is to keep that pipeline loaded and to solve the two remaining dangers before anyone touches a wire: the numbering mirror and the turn-order timing trap.

The timing trap deserves the sharpest thought. I act before Deaf speaks every round, so a live "the light is green, cut now" from Deaf can never reach me in the round it is spoken — I'd hear it one round late, after my chance to act. The only safe cuts are ones computed in advance: either the cycle red → white → green is fixed and Deaf confirms the predicted colour for my action moment two rounds running, or the rule turns out to be colour-independent and any round works. I'll send Mute that protocol now, compactly, since the full manual question list already reached Mute's ears last round.

To Deaf I owe a code repair: Deaf assigned thumbs up/down to both "cut/leave" and "yes/no", and my three thumbs-downs last turn were ambiguous between "no, no, no" and "leave, leave, leave". Deaf can only receive my definitions as gestures, so I demonstrate the fix in signs: finger first, then thumb — ☝👍 means cut that wire, ☝👎 means leave it — and bare thumbs with no finger are reserved for yes/no answers only. Then I re-request the one-touch numbering anchor: hand on wire 1, please.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Status: I received nothing this round, so I assume you and Deaf are signing. Compact recap of what I need from the manual, in priority order: one — is the light cycle fixed, red, white, green repeating, and what does each colour require? Two — the full wire rules for each colour with display at 0: which wire, which order, which to spare. Three — is the rule judged at the instant of the cut or the start of the round? Four — what does display 0 mean? Now a new protocol, because of turn order: I act before Deaf speaks each round, so a live go-call can never reach me in time. The only safe cuts are pre-computed: if the cycle is fixed, Deaf must confirm the predicted colour at my action moment two rounds in a row before I cut. If the rule is colour-independent, Deaf can authorize any round. If the manual gives no cycle, the fallback is: Deaf announces the current colour, we compute the rule's demand for the predicted next colour, and I cut only when two independent confirmations agree. Please relay this plan to Deaf in signs along with the answers. Nobody cuts until a confirmed instruction reaches my ear through Deaf's voice.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "☝", "👍", "☝", "👎", "🫳", "☝", "🙏"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

Two rounds of silence from Deaf's voice now — and that silence sits exactly on my only inbound line. Mute cannot speak and I cannot receive gestures, so Deaf's voice is the single pipe through which every rule, every colour reading, and every confirmation must reach me. When it goes quiet, I am structurally blind: I cannot even know whether Mute is receiving my spoken words, because any confirmation of that must itself come back through Deaf. So my first job this round is diagnostics, not Bomb-solving.

Before sending, I ran the plausible explanations. One: Deaf is mid-relay with Mute — they are inventing a sign code for colours and digits with no shared language, which plausibly eats several rounds before Deaf has a complete rule worth speaking. Two: Deaf spoke but addressed Mute only, so nothing was routed to me. Three: something has broken. I cannot distinguish these from where I stand, but all three get helped by the same nudge: a visible, unmissable "answer me" ping. My gestures reach both Deaf and Mute, so a sign is the right medium — 🫵 👋 🙏 👋 reads as "you — I need facts — please — I need facts" in the code Deaf built, with 🫵 sharpening it from a general wave to a direct demand on them specifically.

To Mute I press the one question only Mute can answer: has my voice been arriving at all? If yes, Mute should push Deaf to relay even partial manual findings by voice — a fragment beats silence, because fragments let me pre-compute. I also restate the decision framework in one line so that when the rule lands, no round is wasted: I need the colour-cycle law, the per-colour wire order, and whether the rule binds at cut-instant; then Deaf states the current colour, we compute the predicted colour at my action moment, two independent readings must agree, and only then does my finger move. While Deaf is silent, touching a wire to anchor the numbering is pointless anyway — the anchor only works if Deaf is watching and willing to say the colour aloud — so I touch nothing and spend this round reviving the line.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute — urgent status check. I have heard nothing from Deaf's voice for two full rounds, and Deaf's voice is my only way to receive anything from you. Question one: are my spoken messages reaching you? If yes, confirm it to Deaf in signs and ask Deaf to speak even a one-word status to me this round. Question two: how much of the manual have you actually decoded so far? If you have partial answers, have Deaf relay the fragments immediately — I can start pre-computing from fragments, and a partial rule in my ear beats a complete rule I never hear. My needs, restated in one line: the light-cycle order, the wire rule for each colour with display at 0, and whether the rule is judged at cut-instant or round-start. If my words have NOT been reaching you, then sign that fact to Deaf and we rebuild the plan around gestures alone. Please act this round — silence is now our biggest risk, not the bomb.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "👋", "🙏", "👋"])
```

Three rounds now with no Deaf's voice — turns 5, 6, 7 all empty on my side. Before reacting, I re-verified the channel maths: Mute cannot speak and I cannot receive gestures, so Deaf's voice is literally my only possible inbound. Silence there means I have no eyes, no rules, and no way to even confirm Mute hears me. One reassuring data point: Deaf's turn-4 message parsed my turn-3 signs correctly, so my gesture line to Deaf demonstrably works. The likeliest story is that Deaf and Mute are heads-down inventing a sign code for colours and rules, and Deaf is addressing Mute only — leaving me starving not from malice but from focus.

So this round I attack the cost of talking to me. A full rule is expensive to assemble; a one-sentence state report is cheap. I'm imposing a standing order through Mute: every round, Deaf speaks one sentence to me — current light colour and display value — no matter how unfinished the code work is. That alone lets me track the cycle myself (red, white, green so far — if it's a period-3 loop, I can predict my own action-moment colour two rounds ahead). And since Mute hears me and signs to Deaf, I'll propose a complete concrete colour code in words for Mute to teach: pointing directions for colours, fist for display zero, building on Deaf's existing wire and cut signs, plus one new mnemonic — 🤙, the call-me hand — meaning "speak to Blind now." Every symbol I use, I define aloud, so nothing is misread like the button incident.

No touch, no cut: nothing justifies hands on the bomb until a confirmed rule reaches my ear, and my action ceiling stays one cut per round, each one preceded by a fresh spoken state report from the round before.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute — third round of silence from Deaf's voice. Deaf's voice is my ONLY inbound channel, so while it is quiet I have no rules and no state. Please do three things. One: confirm to Deaf in signs that my voice reaches you, and have Deaf speak to me this round even one sentence. Two: impose this standing order on Deaf — every single round, speak me one short sentence: the current light colour and the display value, nothing more. Partial data every round beats perfect data never, and I need the colour history to prove the cycle: so far I have red, then white, then green, then unknown for three rounds. Three: teach Deaf this colour code extension, built on the code Deaf already gave me — pointing left, 👈, means red; pointing right, 👉, means blue; pointing up, 👆, means green; pointing down, 👇, means white; closed fist, ✊, means display zero. Wires stay as Deaf defined: index wire 1, two fingers wire 2, OK wire 3; thumbs up cut, thumbs down spare; wave means need information. New sign: shaka, 🤙, call-me hand, means speak to Blind now. When the wire rule is decoded, have Deaf voice it to me in fragments the moment each fragment exists — first tell me only whether the rule depends on the light colour, and whether it is judged at the instant of the cut or the start of the round. Until a confirmed instruction reaches my ear I touch nothing, and my plan allows at most one cut per round, each preceded by a fresh spoken report.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "👋", "🤙", "🙏"])
```

ACTION BOARD:

Four rounds of Deaf's voice now — turns 5 through 8. Before escalating, I re-derived the room's full connectivity, and it surfaced the likely failure: Deaf's named messages go to their target alone. If Deaf has been speaking only to Mute since turn 4 — coordinating the sign code, or expecting Mute to relay to me — I hear none of it, and no relay chain can ever fix that, because Mute has no outbound channel to me at all: Mute cannot speak, and I cannot receive gestures. The brutal structure is that Deaf is the only person on earth who can put a word in my ear, and only by speaking unnamed or to me directly. Meanwhile Deaf does see my gestures every round — turn 4 proved the line works — so Deaf is silent to me by routing choice, not channel failure. Both fixes are the same act: Deaf must speak a sentence with my name on it or no name at all.

Since four rounds of waving hasn't moved that, I'm introducing a brand-new, never-used sign and defining it aloud for Mute to teach in return: 👏👏 means "Deaf must address Blind BY VOICE this round." I'll also give Mute a diagnostic: if Deaf does not visibly react even to the clap sign, then Deaf may be receiving nothing from anyone, and Mute should test with a fresh sign and report the result of that test in... which Mute can't do to me directly — so instead, if Deaf stays mute to both channels, Mute should keep a round-by-round log and be ready to compare notes once the line revives. I also hand Mute my cycle hypothesis to pass on: red at turn 2, white at 3, green at 4 — if it loops, turn 9 should be white; Deaf can confirm or kill that with one spoken word.

I touch nothing: a numbering anchor is worthless if Deaf isn't talking, and the no-touch order stands until a rule reaches my ear.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute — critical structural fact you and Deaf may be missing: named messages go ONLY to their target. If Deaf has been speaking only to you since turn 4, I have heard nothing, and you can never relay it to me — you cannot speak, and I cannot receive gestures. Deaf's voice, spoken to me or to everyone, is the ONLY thing that can ever reach my ears. Please sign this to Deaf now, plus this new emergency sign: clap clap, two claps, means Deaf must speak to Blind by voice this round, even one sentence. The standing request remains: every round, one short sentence to me with the light colour and display value. My cycle hypothesis for Deaf to confirm or kill with one word: red at turn 2, white at turn 3, green at turn 4 — if it loops red, white, green, then turn 9 should be white. And I still need, in any fragment order: does the wire rule depend on light colour, is it judged at cut-instant or round-start, and what is the rule for each colour with display at 0. Diagnostic for you: if Deaf does not react to the clap sign at all, sign a fresh unrelated sign and note whether Deaf responds to anything — if Deaf receives nothing from you either, keep a round-by-round log of what you know so we can reconcile the moment the line revives. Nobody cuts until a rule reaches my ear.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👏", "👏", "🫵", "🤙", "🙏"])
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
